title: Prefill interference nonblocking notes - weekly standup
content:
Daily standup — Prefill interference & non-blocking kernel flow
Date: 2026-10-21 09:30 PT
Owner: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Marcus, Lina, Omar, Jules, several SREs on rotation

Purpose
- Capture progress on the non-blocking handoff prototype that interleaves prefill work and live KV traffic
- Surface telemetry anomalies for the StaggerWindow v2 experiments
- Decide next experiment and who will own rollout gating

Quick summary
- Experiment Interleave-1427 (staggered prefill + non-blocking kernel handoff) ran across two r3 clusters (night window) and produced mixed results: throughput improved for background-prefill traffic, but p99 token latency regressed by ~15ms in microbatch-heavy workloads.
- Root cause appears correlated with the new reordering step that can occasionally create transient KV read amplification when shadow-cache lookups fall back to host memory.
- Non-blocking handoff code path is stable — no crashes — but needs an extra guard to limit simultaneous reorders per-core.

Telemetry highlights (night run, 02:00–05:00 PT)
- Controlled baseline: StaggerWindow v1 + baseline kernel
  - aggregate throughput: 1.04x baseline
  - p50 token latency: -4ms
  - p95 token latency: +2ms
  - p99 token latency: +15ms under 45% microbatch ratio
- Interleave-1427:
  - background-prefill success rate: +18% (less evict thrash)
  - seen KV read duplicates per-request: median 1.02 -> 1.18 (indicates amplification spikes)
  - tail CPU scheduling delay spikes coincident with reorder flushes

Observed behaviors and hypotheses
- Hypothesis A: The reorder flush allows multiple prefills to touch the same KV shard concurrently, which increases hot-key read amplification and creates CPU contention on the sampler threads.
- Hypothesis B: Memory allocator fragmentation in the shadow-cache path increases latency jitter under microbatching; mitigated in tests that used the jemalloc tune profile.
- Hypothesis C: Non-blocking handoff defers some locks to per-core queues; in high-coalesce mode, queue lengths spike and cause unexpected backpressure into the kernel scheduler.

Repro steps attempted
- Re-run Interleave-1427 with jemalloc tuned (background): reduced p99 regression by ~6ms.
- Added per-shard inflight cap (soft cap=8) to reorder step: removed worst p99 spikes but reduced background-prefill success by ~6%.
- Isolated single-shard synthetic test: reproduced read duplication without kernel scheduling load, suggesting multiple actors touching same KV index is core issue.

Decision items (today)
- Keep Interleave-1427 paused for rollout until we implement per-core reorder throttling (Jules).
- Run focused experiment that combines jemalloc tuning + per-shard inflight cap + lower coalesce window (Marcus).
- Create a telemetry dashboard spike-alert for KV read-duplicate ratio and reorder queue depth (SRE on-call: Omar).

Action items
- Aisha: Draft short memo for PMs explaining why enabled prefill interleaving increased cold-cache stability but introduced tail regressions. Due: 2026-10-23.
- Marcus: Launch a controlled canary (2 nodes) with jemalloc profile + inflight cap = 6; monitor 12h night run. Jira ENG-1435. Due: 2026-10-24.
- Jules: Implement per-core reorder-throttle (rate-limiter) and add an opt-in flag in runtime config. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/2911. Due: 2026-10-27.
- Lina: Add synthetic single-shard harness to reproduce amplification locally (docker image + runbook). Put artifacts in /tmp/ci-prefill. Due: 2026-10-22.
- Omar (SRE): Add Prometheus rule and pager threshold for KV read-dup ratio > 1.12 sustained for 3m. Due: 2026-10-22.

Open questions
- What is the acceptable background-prefill success drop when preserving p99 for user-facing requests? Product wants >12% improvement, but SREs say p99 regressions must be <8ms. Need product tradeoff guidance.
- Could a small amount of write-side batching reduce read amplification by coalescing prefill writes? (Discuss with platform-engineering.)
- Is there an alternative allocator or per-thread memory pool we can use that avoids jemalloc tuning in production?

Notes & experiments to archive
- Experiment Interleave-1427: artifacts saved -> s3://redwood-experiments/prefill/interleave-1427/ (profiles + traces).
- jemalloc tune run: patch applied locally on canary nodes; see PR notes and flamegraphs attached in linked PR.

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: If reorder queue lock takes longer, handoff may induce transient rate-limit cascades. Mitigation: add circuit-breaker to fallback to serial prefill for affected shards.
- Risk: Telemetry visibility gap for multiple short-lived spikes. Mitigation: add histogram buckets that capture duplicate-read slices by shard id in 10s windows.

Meeting notes (decision log)
- 09:55: unanimous: do not roll Interleave-1427 to prod.
- 10:05: agreed to fast-follow with limited canary and allocator tuning before any further expansion.

Next sync
- Mini-handoff-review on 2026-10-22 16:00 PT (30m) to check canary results and PR status. Invite: eng-serving-runtime, platform-eng liaison.

References
- Related ticket: ENG-1427 (prefill interleaving design)
- PRs: #2896 (initial handoff), #2911 (throttle WIP)

Notes to self
- Snapshot current kernel trace collection settings; we might need to bump sample rate for the reorder path only.
- Keep a short list of shards that reproduced locally for quicker reruns.

-- end of standup notes --
